content: The Jardine Water Purification Plant, previously known as the Central District Filtration Plant, is recognized as the largest water filtration facility in the world. It is situated at 1000 East Ohio Street, just north of Navy Pier in Chicago, Illinois. The plant sources raw water from two of Chicago's water cribs located far offshore in Lake Michigan. It processes and delivers nearly one billion gallons of water daily to consumers residing in the northern and central regions of the city. The construction of the plant began in the 1960s, and it became operational in 1968. Shortly after its completion, the Ohio Street Beach naturally formed in the bay area created by the plant's structure. The landscaping surrounding the facility, as well as the adjacent Milton Olive Park, was designed by the renowned landscape architect Dan Kiley. Additionally, the front entrance of the plant is adorned with a statue titled Hymn to Water, created by the artist Milton Horn. The southern portion of Chicago is served by a separate facility, the South Water Purification Plant. Together, these two plants provide water to approximately 5 million residents within the city and an additional 118 suburban communities.
